taxonomyNote: NatureServe (Burbrink et al. 2011) splits L. pyromelana into northern L. pyromelana and southern L. knoblochi; its habitat text is based mainly on L. pyromelana.
fieldMarks: Coral-snake mimic with white crossbands where a coral snake has yellow.
behavior: Generally diurnal but may be most active late afternoon, evening and dusk.
Diet includes lizards and presumably snakes and small mammals.
habitat: Rocky montane habitat often near streams or springs, and mesic canyons at lower elevation; pinyon-juniper, oak-juniper, pine-oak or pine-Douglas-fir woodland, or chaparral.
By day found among rocks, logs or dense vegetation.
range: Sierra Madre Occidental in eastern Sonora and western Chihuahua, north to the Madrean Sky Islands of southern Arizona and southwestern New Mexico.
